heroHeadline: Assembly Unanimously Passes First Vote on 'Traitors' Election Ban as Rubio Calls It a 'Legislative Sham' and Peru Invokes Democratic Charter
heroSubtitle: Nicaragua's National Assembly unanimously approved the first-round passage of a constitutional reform on September 1 barring anyone designated a 'traitor to the homeland' from office and extending terms from six to seven years, with ratification set for a second vote beginning January 18, 2027; Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the vote a 'legislative sham' on September 2, and Peru's foreign ministry followed on September 3 with a formal communique branding the reform a 'flagrant violation' of the Inter-American Democratic Charter and urging OAS/UN action
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
